accuracy.evidence: Prefix meanings and the spelling rule checked against the DfE National Curriculum in England, English Appendix 1 (Spelling), Years 3–4: prefixes un-, dis-, mis- (negative meanings), re- (again or back), super-, anti-, auto-, with 'most prefixes are added to the beginning of root words without any changes in spelling' and the examples disappoint, misbehave, redo, superstar, antiseptic, autograph; meanings cross-checked in the Oxford Children's Dictionary and Merriam-Webster (pre- before, anti- against, auto- self, super- above/more than). Every spelling in the lab and items was checked: misspell, dissatisfied (double letter at the join), disappear, mistake (single s); fake prefixes dish, ready, reach, mister leave non-words. Letter-count items (mis- +3, super- +5, dis- −3) and the reread count (n + 1) were checked at every parameter corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors for prefixes: dropping a letter at the join (step 2 prediction mispell, feedback 'You lost a letter', challenge tags lost and root, p2); adding a letter (dissappear, disatisfied/misstake feedback 'You added a letter', tag extra, m7); choosing a prefix with the wrong meaning (step 1 feedback naming each prefix's meaning, tags wrongly, again, re, neg); auto- read as car (step 4 prediction, tag car, m4); and treating any word that starts with the same letters as prefixed (step 5 prediction about dish, tag fake, p5, m6).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpfx covers this topic's own set of seven prefixes and its spelling join: prefix tiles are clipped onto a root to fit a meaning clue, the join is spelled by choosing between double- and single-letter forms with feedback that counts the letters at the seam, words are filed into not/wrongly/again/before boxes, anti-/auto-/super- words are matched to meanings, and words are tested by removing the letters. It differs from the un- lab (one prefix, pictures), the word-families lab (one root, suffix jobs) and the hyphens lab; the lab_distinct gate passes it under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Tapping pre for 'play it again' says pre means before and play-again needs re-; tapping mispell explains that mis ends in s and spell starts with s, so both stay; filing unfair under 'before' names the prefix's real meaning; choosing 'a graph about cars' explains auto- means self; and judging dislike as a fake shows 'like' is left, a real word. The finished build step lists replay, dislike, misread and preheat with each meaning beside it.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options: 'One: mispell' for mis + spell (the spelling cards then only accept misspell), 'A graph about cars' for autograph (the match only accepts 'your own name, written by you'), and 'Yes: it starts with dis' for dish (taking dis off leaves h, which the sort rejects).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge items whose wrong options each carry a tagged message naming the slip: wrongly (mis- for not), again (re- for not), lost (one s in misspell), root (a letter dropped from the root word), extra (two s in disappear), re (again for pre-), neg (not for pre-), fake (ready and reach only start with r-e), car (auto- as car) and super (big is super-, not auto-).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the family readability limits: kid text Flesch-Kincaid 2.5 (limit 5.0), adult 9.7 (limit 10). Kid paragraphs use short sentences and give one example word per prefix; lab step texts are two or three very short sentences, and every prefix is shown in its own colour on the canvas.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches. Each step does one job (choose by meaning, spell the join, sort by meaning, big prefixes, fake prefixes), feedback states the exact letters involved, and each item explanation gives the rule in one or two sentences.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px touch in light and dark for each step before and after Show me, plus scrolled single-frame checks: prefix tiles are 52 px tall in one row, the two spelling cards and the two big piles are thumb-sized, the young style gives 56 px buttons below, and the canvas stays light in dark mode so the coloured prefix and root letters keep their contrast. After the first screenshots the meaning bins were redrawn with the prefix in the heading so two words fit in each box, the canvas was shortened, and the finished build step now lists all four words.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap has a button: re-/dis-/mis-/pre- (aria-label gives each meaning), both spellings (aria-label spells the word letter by letter), not/wrongly/again/before labelled with the current word, both meanings, and 'prefix + word' / 'just starts that way'. The canvas aria-label reads the current word or clue and the last feedback after every move; challenge feedback is an aria-live status; walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.

sources: Department for Education, National Curriculum in England: English Appendix 1 (Spelling), Years 3–4 prefixes
Common Core State Standards ELA L.3.4b and L.4.4b (affixes as clues to meaning)
Oxford Children's Dictionary and Merriam-Webster: meanings of dis-, mis-, re-, pre-, anti-, auto-, super-
